title: Erlang Quiz
description: Review the 12 starter lessons. The questions name the example to revisit. Take your time, use the lessons, and read the reason after each answer.

questions.question: io:format writes output. ~n starts a new line. The module exports main so the command can call it. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: io:format reads the format string. ~n starts a newline after the greeting. The module name lesson must match lesson.erl.

questions.question: Variables start with a capital letter. A variable can be bound only once in a function call. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: Pencils binds to 3. The argument list gives its sum with 2 to the ~p slot. Matching a bound variable to a different value causes an error.

questions.question: Atoms are fixed labels. An unquoted atom usually starts with a lower-case letter. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: ready is an atom. The ~p format shows the atom value. Names starting with capitals are variables, not atoms.

questions.question: A tuple can hold a status and a result. Pattern matching pulls its parts into names. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The tuple pattern matches ok and binds Score to 8. The tuple shape and first atom must match.

questions.question: [Head | Tail] separates the first item from the rest of a list. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The head-tail pattern puts 4 in First. The remaining list is ignored. An empty list cannot match a head-and-tail pattern.

questions.code:
-module(lesson).
-export([main/0]).
main() ->
    Book = #{title => "Moon Trip", pages => 24},
    io:format("~s~n", [maps:get(title, Book)]).
questions.question: A map keeps key-value pairs. maps:get reads the value for a key. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: maps:get selects the title entry. ~s prints its string characters. A missing key needs a fallback or an explicit check.

questions.code:
-module(lesson).
-export([main/0]).
main() ->
    Light = green,
    Message = case Light of red -> "Stop"; green -> "Go"; _ -> "Wait" end,
    io:format("~s~n", [Message]).
questions.question: case compares a value with patterns. The first matching branch supplies the result. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The green branch matches, so Message becomes Go. Use semicolons between branches and end after the last branch.

questions.code:
-module(lesson).
-export([main/0]).
main() ->
    Score = 8,
    Message = case Score of N when N >= 5 -> "Pass"; _ -> "Try again" end,
    io:format("~s~n", [Message]).
questions.question: A guard adds a small test after a pattern. when introduces that test. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The guard accepts 8 because it is at least 5. Not every function is allowed inside a guard.

questions.question: A named function can take an input and return its final expression. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: twice receives 4 and returns 8 to the printing call. End each function definition with a period.

questions.question: A list comprehension visits values and builds a result for each one. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The comprehension takes 2 then 3, doubles them, and collects both results. Use <- to take values from a list inside the comprehension.

questions.code:
-module(lesson).
-export([main/0]).
main() ->
    self() ! {score, 8},
    receive {score, N} -> io:format("~p~n", [N]) end.
questions.question: A process has a mailbox. ! sends a message, and receive reads a matching message. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: self() names this process. The tuple is sent to its mailbox, then receive extracts 8. receive waits if no message matches; real waiting code often needs after.

questions.code:
-module(lesson).
-export([main/0]).
main() ->
    Parent = self(),
    spawn(fun() -> Parent ! {answer, 4 * 2} end),
    receive {answer, N} -> io:format("~p~n", [N]) end.
questions.question: spawn starts a new process. It can send a result back to the parent process. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
questions.explanation: The spawned process calculates 8 and sends it to Parent. The parent waits for that answer. Processes have their own data; share results with messages.
